Home / Insurance types / Compulsory motor
Legal requirement

TRNC compulsory motor insurance

Every motor vehicle used on the road in Northern Cyprus must hold this policy. It pays for the damage you cause to other people — it does not cover your own vehicle. The legal basis is Chapter 333, the Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Law.

Last updated: September 2026 · Sources at the foot of the page

Cover limits

Property damageSingle event or chain collision
1,200,000 ₺
Death and injuryPrivate vehicles
8,000,000 ₺
Death and injuryCommercial vehicles
15,000,000 ₺

The property damage limit was raised from 800,000 ₺ to 1,200,000 ₺ by regulation on 25 February 2026 (Official Gazette no. 41, Annex III). Limits can change by amendment to the law or regulations.

Common mistake

Your home country's arrangements do not apply here

  • A green card does not work. The TRNC is not a member of the green card system. Green cards issued in the EU or in Turkey are not valid here, and none is issued for a TRNC-registered vehicle.
  • EU consumer mechanisms do not apply. TRNC insurers are not within EU insurance schemes.
  • The Republic of Cyprus Financial Ombudsman has no jurisdiction here. A complaint about a TRNC policy cannot be taken to it.
  • A policy bought in another country does not cover a TRNC-registered vehicle. If you have bought a vehicle here, you need a policy from a company licensed here.

Complaints go to the Insurance Arbitration Commission, which sits within KKSRSB (Kuzey Kıbrıs Sigorta ve Reasürans Şirketleri Birliği, the North Cyprus Association of Insurance and Reinsurance Companies) and accepts applications through its own form.

Cover

What it covers and what it does not

✓ Covers

  • ·Repair of the other party's vehicle
  • ·Towing costs
  • ·Death or permanent disability of third parties
  • ·Emergency medical treatment costs
  • ·Other property damage caused to third parties — walls, kerbs, electricity poles

✕ Does not cover

  • ·Damage to your own vehicle — comprehensive motor insurance (kasko) is needed for that
  • ·Damage arising during racing or test driving
  • ·Driving without a licence
  • ·Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs

The full list of exclusions is in the policy general conditions. KKSRSB publishes these in Turkish and English. Both are official texts, not translations — read the English one directly.

Pricing

Prices are not free to move

A minimum premium is set by vehicle use class and no company may quote below that floor. Companies must notify the Department of Money, Exchange and Development Fund Affairs and Kuzey Kıbrıs Sigorta Bilgi Merkezi (KKSBM, the North Cyprus Insurance Information Centre) at least 10 days before applying a new tariff.

What this means in practice: shopping for the cheapest quote achieves little. The difference between companies shows up in service, not in price.

No-claims discount. A bonus-malus (step) system operates in the TRNC and records are held at KKSBM. The number of steps and the discount rates are not published in any public source — so no rate is given here. Rates from other countries do not apply.

Six companies do both — an English interface and an end-to-end online policy: Aveon, Can, Creditwest, Dağlı, GİG and Limasol.

A further company presents English pages that our data marks as machine-translated; it is not counted in the 17.

If an uninsured vehicle hits you

The Guarantee Fund steps in

The Guarantee Fund within KKSRSB covers loss caused by uninsured vehicles, unlicensed drivers and hit-and-run vehicles.

Applications are made through a lawyer and the lawyer's fee is paid by the Fund. There is no cost to the applicant.

Documents needed

  • ·Police accident report
  • ·Photographs of the damage
  • ·Vehicle damage assessment
  • ·Doctor's report if there is injury
  • ·Any invoices relating to the loss

Guarantee Fund application information

Gaps

Three things we are not going to state

The penalty for driving uninsured. Set by Article 17 of Chapter 333. The figures in that article are not legible in the public PDF of the law and we found no current figure in any other official source. Almost every number returned by a search for this belongs to another country's legislation. We would rather leave it blank.

No-claims discount rates. A step system exists and the records are held at KKSBM, but the number of steps and the rates are not published anywhere public.

Whether a foreign driving licence affects your cover. This matters to anyone who bought a vehicle here on a home-country licence, and we could not settle it. In a 2022 press report the president of the Rental Car Operators Union said that people without a TRNC licence are treated as unlicensed and "insurance does not cover them"; in the same report the Director of the Traffic Department said a licence is accepted for as long as the residence permit runs. These are press statements, not official texts, and they contradict each other. Driving without a licence is an exclusion in the general conditions, so the question is a real one. Ask your insurer in writing before you rely on the answer.
